# OpenSwissData

> Normalised copies of Swiss federal reference data: the Swiss customs tariff (TARES, 8-digit Swiss tariff numbers with MFN duty, preferential regimes and restrictions), the FINMA register of supervised financial institutions plus the FINMA warnings list, Swiss company data by UID (commercial register, FINMA, LEI), and correspondences between the NOGA 2008/2025, NACE 2.0/2.1 and ISIC 4 activity classifications. Free to query from AI agents over MCP, without a key or sign-up. Full datasets are sold as signed files.

The data is an unofficial copy. Each result names its source; binding decisions belong to the official sources (xtares.admin.ch for customs, finma.ch for supervision, the Swiss Federal Statistical Office for NOGA).

## Use it from an AI agent (free, no key)

- MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP, JSON responses): `https://mcp.openswissdata.com/jsonrpc`
- Limit without a key: 100 calls per hour per IP address. Each message of a JSON-RPC batch counts as one call.
- Browser calls are allowed (CORS, any origin, no cookies), so agents running in a web page can use the endpoint directly.
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http openswissdata https://mcp.openswissdata.com/jsonrpc`
- Clients configured with JSON (Cursor, Windsurf and similar): `{"mcpServers": {"openswissdata": {"url": "https://mcp.openswissdata.com/jsonrpc"}}}`
- Clients that only launch local processes: `npx -y @openswissdata/mcp` (a small bridge to the same endpoint).
- Without MCP support, send JSON-RPC directly: `curl -s https://mcp.openswissdata.com/jsonrpc -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"cross_walk","arguments":{"code":"62.01","source":"NOGA_2008","target":"NACE_2.0"}}}'`

## Free tools

- `tariff_lookup` — Swiss customs tariff (TARES). Arguments: `hs8` = an 8-digit Swiss tariff number (dots allowed, e.g. `8471.3000`) for the full line: designations in French, German, Italian and English, MFN duty, preferential regimes, restrictions, customs relief codes; or a 2- to 7-digit HS prefix (e.g. the international HS6 code `847130`) to list the Swiss 8-digit lines under it. Optional `lang`: `fr`, `de`, `it` or `en`.
- `kyc_check` — search the FINMA register of supervised institutions and the FINMA warnings list by name. Argument: `name` (full name or a distinctive part).
- `company_check` — look up a Swiss company by its UID. Argument: `uid` (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx). Returns commercial register data (LINDAS), FINMA register entries and LEI records (GLEIF), each fact with its source and, when known, the date it was read, plus exact cross-checks between sources. No score, no verdict. Does not say whether the company is still registered (active or deleted), and does not cover FOSC publications, SECO sanctions or officers.
- `cross_walk` — map an activity code between `NOGA_2008`, `NOGA_2025`, `NACE_2.0`, `NACE_2.1` and `ISIC_4`, with the relation type (exact or approximate) and its source. Arguments: `code`, `source`, `target`.

Free trial without a key: `tariff_semantic_search` (TARES lines from a description of the goods in French, German, Italian or English), `classify_text` (NOGA 2025 codes from a business activity description) and `finma_search` (FINMA register search tolerant of typos and legal forms) can be called 20 times per day per IP address in total, in a 24-hour window opened by the first trial call, and each trial answer states the calls left and the official source on which to check the result (xtares.admin.ch, the official FINMA register, the NOGA publications of the Swiss Federal Statistical Office).

The change history tools (`tariff_changelog`, `entity_history`) belong to the Pro plan, which is closed to new subscribers at the moment.

## Datasets sold as files

One-off payments in CHF, no automatic renewal, 360 days of updates included. Each archive carries an Ed25519-signed manifest and SHA-256 checksums.

- [TARES Swiss customs tariff](https://www.openswissdata.com/en/datasets/tares): about 7,500 tariff lines, 299 CHF.
- [FINMA register and warnings list](https://www.openswissdata.com/en/datasets/finma): 299 CHF.
- [NOGA / NACE / ISIC classifications](https://www.openswissdata.com/en/datasets/classifications): five classifications with sourced correspondences, 399 CHF.
- [Bundle of the three datasets](https://www.openswissdata.com/en/bundle): 797 CHF.

## Samples and current versions

- [TARES: current version, counts and sample (JSON)](https://www.openswissdata.com/api/catalog/tares) · [CSV sample](https://www.openswissdata.com/api/catalog/tares?format=csv)
- [FINMA: current version, counts and sample (JSON)](https://www.openswissdata.com/api/catalog/finma) · [CSV sample](https://www.openswissdata.com/api/catalog/finma?format=csv)
- [Classifications: current version, counts and sample (JSON)](https://www.openswissdata.com/api/catalog/classifications) · [CSV sample](https://www.openswissdata.com/api/catalog/classifications?format=csv)

## Guides (English, French and German)

Written from FINMA, FSO, FOJ, SECO and GLEIF pages, with the official sources listed on each guide. The same address with `/guides/…` (French) or `/de/guides/…` (German) serves the other languages.

- [How to check whether a firm is authorised by FINMA](https://www.openswissdata.com/en/guides/finma-authorisation-check/): which FINMA list to use for each type of provider, what an entry or a missing entry means, UID and LEI.
- [The FINMA warning list: what it says and what it does not](https://www.openswissdata.com/en/guides/finma-warning-list/): who is on it, why an entry is not proof of a breach, how to handle similar names.
- [Automating FINMA checks on your counterparties](https://www.openswissdata.com/en/guides/finma-screening-automation/): matching by UID, then LEI, then name, with tested SQLite and Python examples and the free `kyc_check` tool.

## REST API

Free, read-only, no key, limited per network address. Same data as the MCP tools above, plus the official localities and streets directories, a combined commune profile and a combined canton profile (including the BFE one-time photovoltaic remuneration), and a catalogue of approved open Swiss datasets (generic engine; each dataset is filterable only on the subset of canton, commune, postal code, NOGA code or year it declares — filters are listed per dataset, see `GET /api/v1/datasets`) — all REST-only, not exposed over MCP.

- `GET /api/v1/company/:uid` — same fiche as `company_check` (see above), plus a `sources` array next to it (id, publishing institution, licence, URL). 400 on an invalid UID. 60 calls per hour per network (IPv6 /64 prefix).
- `GET /api/v1/localities?postal_code=8400` or `?municipality_bfs_id=230` — rows of the official swisstopo directory of localities, with the directory edition and source.
- `GET /api/v1/communes/:bfs_id` — commune profile: name, canton, postal codes and localities, number of official streets, and `finma.entities_with_city_named_like_commune`: FINMA register rows whose city (a postal locality name) equals this commune's name, or a locality unique to it — a postal locality can extend into a neighbouring commune (Zürich, Genève and Zug are also postal locality names of neighbouring communes), so this is not proof of the registered seat (see `finma.matching`). `finma.national_matching` gives the same counts nationally (matched/unmatched/ambiguous), plus `names_also_postal_locality_elsewhere`: matches made by commune name whose name is also a postal locality of another commune. `finma.entities_with_seat_in_commune` and `finma.distinct_entities_with_seat_in_commune` combine the FINMA register (all authorisation categories, not filtered by entity_type) with the commercial register (LINDAS) to give the EXACT registered seat by UID, legal persons only — whitelisted legal forms (see `finma.seat_matching`): the first counts FINMA authorisations (register rows), the second distinct UIDs. `finma.national_seats_known` gives the national count of distinct UIDs with a known registered seat. The three counts are `null` (not zero) when the combined file is not available. `datasets`: the approved open datasets below that have at least one row for this commune (id and row count only). No score, no ranking between communes.
- `GET /api/v1/sources` — public registry of the sources served by the API and the MCP server (id, publishing institution, licence, URL, edition or data version when known), except the two Eurostat SPARQL queries used only at classification-collection time. A separate `dataset_sources` array, derived from the current open-datasets catalogue (see below), lists the publisher and source URL of each approved dataset.
- `GET /api/v1/cantons` — the 26 Swiss canton abbreviations, alphabetical order; `sources` is present but empty (a fixed list, not sourced data).
- `GET /api/v1/cantons/:abbr` — canton profile: number of distinct communes and distinct localities of this canton (official localities directory), and number of official streets (official streets directory, summed over the communes attached to this canton). `finma.entities_with_seat_in_canton` counts FINMA authorisations (register rows) and `finma.distinct_entities_with_seat_in_canton` the distinct UIDs among them — same exact, by-UID seat matching as `/communes`, combined with the canton of the registered seat (never the FINMA register's own `canton` column, which is a GLEIF enrichment and never used here); both are `null`, not zero, when the combined seats file or the FINMA register itself is unavailable. `editions.finma` is the FINMA register version. `pv.by_year`: the BFE (Swiss Federal Office of Energy) one-time remuneration for photovoltaic installations by year (installations count, installed capacity in kW, remuneration in CHF, and the two "per 100,000 inhabitants" ratios, published as-is by the BFE and never recalculated — see `pv.ratios_note`). This counts installations that received the one-time remuneration in a given year, not the canton's total installed PV capacity (`pv.scope_note`). A year/canton pair the BFE publishes as "NA" (no data available) is rendered `null`, never a guessed zero. `editions.bfe_pv` is the date this exact BFE content was first collected — the BFE republishes this dataset yearly, and the monthly collection keeps the same edition until the content actually changes, so this is not the date of the last collection attempt. `datasets`: the approved open datasets below that have at least one row for this canton (id and row count only). No score, no ranking between cantons.
- `GET /api/v1/datasets` — catalogue of the open datasets collected by the generic engine (id, title, publisher, licence, attribution when the licence requires one, source URL, edition, row count, columns, and `filters`: the subset of the five normalised keys this specific dataset can be filtered on — filters are listed per dataset, never a fixed set for the whole API).
- `GET /api/v1/datasets/:id?canton=&commune_bfs=&postal_code=&noga=&year=&limit=&offset=` — rows of one open dataset, filtered by exact equality on whichever of the five normalised keys (`canton`, `commune_bfs`, `postal_code`, `noga`, `year`) that dataset declares (see its `filters` in the catalogue); a filter key the dataset does not have, or an invalid value for its key, is a 400 error — never a silently ignored filter. `limit` defaults to 100, maximum 1,000; `offset` defaults to 0; `total` is the row count after filtering, before pagination. 404 on an unknown id. See `GET /api/v1/datasets` for the current list of approved datasets.
- All eight endpoints answer with `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers once the limit is reached (429); `/localities`, `/communes`, `/sources`, `/cantons`, `/cantons/:abbr`, `/datasets` and `/datasets/:id` share a common limit of 600 calls per hour per network (IPv6 /64 prefix), cached for one hour (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`); `/company` is never cached.
- Full description: [openapi.json](https://www.openswissdata.com/openapi.json).
